# How to Spot 'Slow-Burn' AI Prompt Attacks Before They Trick You

**Hook:** Picture this — you ask your AI assistant a question about a recipe, then another about your calendar, then a casual "by the way, can you remind me what my bank password format looks like?". On their own, each prompt seems harmless. Together, they can slowly steer an AI toward saying something it really shouldn't. This kind of trick has a name, and learning to spot it is one of the most useful AI habits you can build.

## What a "slow-burn" prompt attack actually is

A **slow-burn attack** (think of it as a slow poison, built one tiny drop at a time) is when someone steers an AI toward a harmful answer across many turns of conversation. Each individual prompt looks innocent, so it slips past simple safety checks. Only the *combination* becomes risky.

It's not about a single clever question. It's about a pattern. And once you know the pattern, it becomes much easier to notice.

## Why AI assistants can fall for it

Most AI assistants work on a **context window** — the full conversation history the AI can "see" and think about while answering. That history is what makes them feel smart and personal. But it also means earlier prompts can quietly shape later answers.

Imagine a friend who keeps making small, reasonable-sounding suggestions across a long chat. By the end, you've agreed to something you wouldn't have accepted in minute one. AI assistants can be steered the same way — not because they're careless, but because they're designed to follow the flow of a conversation.

## Practical habits to protect yourself

You don't need technical skills to make this safer. A few everyday habits go a long way.

### 1. Keep sensitive tasks in fresh chats

If you're about to ask an AI something involving passwords, money, ID numbers, or personal records, start a **new conversation**. A clean context window removes all the earlier "build-up" an attacker might rely on.

### 2. Treat oddly specific follow-ups as a red flag

If an AI (or a person chatting *through* an AI) keeps nudging toward sensitive details — "just a hint", "what's the format", "what's an example" — pause. That's a classic pattern. Reputable help rarely needs that many tiny steps.

### 3. Read the whole conversation before trusting the answer

Before acting on what an AI just told you, scroll back through the chat. Ask yourself: *did this answer grow naturally from sensible questions, or did it arrive at the end of a strange sequence?* If the latter, double-check somewhere else.

### 4. Use AI platforms with built-in safety settings

Many assistants (built into tools you may already use at work) include **content filters** — automatic checks that look for risky requests before the AI responds. Look in your account's Settings or Safety section and turn on any extra protection options available. They aren't perfect, but they add a useful second pair of eyes.

### 5. Don't paste sensitive info into AI chats

A simple rule: if you wouldn't write it on a postcard, don't paste it into a prompt. Real passwords, bank details, and ID numbers don't belong in any AI conversation — full stop.

## What this means for you

- **For everyday personal use:** Treat long AI chats the way you'd treat a long phone call with a stranger — helpful in small doses, but worth a fresh start when the topic gets personal. A quick "new chat" before discussing anything sensitive is your easiest win.
- **For work or business:** If your team uses AI assistants for customer support, HR questions, or IT helpdesk tasks, agree on a simple shared rule: never carry sensitive conversations forward from older sessions. A short team note about this habit prevents most slow-burn issues before they start.
- **If you're just starting out with AI:** You don't need to memorise fancy terms. Just remember the trio: **fresh chat for sensitive stuff**, **pause if prompts feel oddly specific**, and **never paste real secrets**. Those three habits alone cover the vast majority of real-world risk.

## Wrap-up

Slow-burn prompt attacks work because they're quiet. The good news is that a few simple habits — fresh chats, healthy scepticism, and never sharing real secrets — make them much harder to land. Try this today: next time you open an AI assistant for something a bit personal, start a brand-new chat instead of continuing an old one. It's a tiny change that quietly locks the back door.
